userStories.title: Engine client and live handler
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Establish the engine request client, pure helpers, project-id resolver, permission predicate and project live event.

**Motivation** — An agent write that a policy holds for a human (any of the 126 gated routes) shows up in no web inbox.

**Approach** — **The list API does not return fleet detail fields; details load for the open row.**
- `ApprovalRequestSummaryDto` has no `input`, `jobId` or `details`. The inbox shows each row from summary fields:
  - the key label;
  - the requester;
  - the project;
  - the countdown.
- It fetches `GET /approvals/:id` only for the row it opens.
- The two surfaces that need a field from `input` fetch the detail per row through `useApprovalInbox().listDetailed(filters, limit)`:
  - the job page, for its command previews;
  - the budget banner, for its `policyId`.
- `listDetailed` details only the first `limit` rows in the order it is given (`DETAIL_FETCH_LIMIT = 20`). A row past the limit, or one whose detail fetch fails, has `detail: null` and shows the key label.

**Who sees which controls comes from the row, not from the caller's keys.**
- `.nax/rules/web.md` says to gate a control on the key its route requires. Here that key is `approval.decide`, and the API checks it per request: pattern, `approverMustHoldAction`, self mode. The browser cannot repeat that check.
- `GET /approvals` already returns only the requests the caller may see. That is their own requests plus everything their decide scopes cover, narrowed patterns included.
- So `viewerActions(request, userId)` decides from the row alone.
- The caller is the **requester** when `actorType === 'USER'` and `actorId === userId`:
  - a pending own request shows Cancel;
  - it shows the decide controls only when `requiredMode === 'self'`.
- Every other pending request shows the decide controls and no Cancel. A settled request shows neither.
- A refused decide surfaces through `extractApiError`, as `web.md` requires.

**`PermissionSet.mayDecide()`.** The nav and the palette need to know "may decide something". That is either `approval.decide` or any narrowed `approval.decide@<pattern>` key, which `has()` cannot answer. `permissionSet` gains `mayDecide()`; `EMPTY_PERMISSIONS.mayDecide()` answers `false`.

**Key labels.** `requestKeyLabel(t, te, key)` answers `approvals.keys.<key with '.' replaced by '_'>` when that i18n key exists, else the raw key. Only the two fleet keys get labels in this feature.

**Visibility also includes `onBehalfOf` rows.** `GET /approvals` also returns requests raised on the caller's behalf. `viewerActions` gives those the decide controls; the API may refuse, and the refusal toasts.

**`listForJob(jobId)`** returns `JobApprovalRow[]`. It lists with `{ jobId, size: '100' }` and orders the rows: pending first by soonest `expiresAt`, then the rest newest first. It then details the first `DETAIL_FETCH_LIMIT` rows through `listDetailed`.

Create lib/approval-requests.ts, composables/useApprovalInbox.ts and composables/useProjectRef.ts. buildRequestQuery returns pending status and size 100, or All size 20 with current only after page 1, plus supplied projectId. sortPendingRequests orders expiresAt ascending. The client uses useApi.$api for GET /approvals, GET /approvals/counts, GET /approvals/:id, POST /approvals/:id/decisions and POST /approvals/:id/cancel. Keep list pagination metadata. Both successful mutations increase approvalRequestsVersion. useProjectRef(slug).load() resolves GET /projects/:slug to its id; callers handle presentation errors. Add LiveApprovalRequestEvent, parseApprovalRequestEvent and optional onApprovalRequest to the stream; attach its listener only when the handler is given, and forward it through the hub alongside existing fleet handlers. Do not remove fleet_approval. Add approvals.keys labels for fleet_job_shell_escalate and fleet_budget_override, approvals.comment.tooLong and whole-approvals English/Chinese parity tests. buildCommentSchema(t) enforces MAX_REQUEST_COMMENT=2000; body inclusion trims and omits blank comments.

**Scope** — In: engine foundation, permissions predicate, stream/hub, key labels/comment schema and foundation tests. Out: inbox UI (US-002), submission panel (US-003), fleet adapters/panels (US-004), toasts/badge/nav (US-005–006), consumer rewrites (US-007), policy UI (US-008–009), deletion (US-010).

**Interface** — `ApprovalRequestSummary`, `ApprovalRequestDetail`, `ApprovalRequestCounts`, `RequestStatus`; `buildRequestQuery`, `sortPendingRequests`, `viewerActions`, `inboxHref`, `requestKeyLabel`, `buildCommentSchema`, `MAX_REQUEST_COMMENT`, `DETAIL_FETCH_LIMIT`; `useApprovalInbox`, `approvalRequestsVersion`; `useProjectRef`; `LiveApprovalRequestEvent`, `parseApprovalRequestEvent`, `ProjectEventHandlers.onApprovalRequest`. `useApprovalInbox` provides `list`, `listForJob`, `listDetailed`, `get`, `counts`, `decide` and `cancel`, and the `approvalRequestsVersion` ref. `mayDecide(): boolean`; `onApprovalRequest?: (event: LiveApprovalRequestEvent) => void`; `JobApprovalRow = { request: ApprovalRequestSummary; detail: ApprovalRequestDetail | null }`. Summary fields are id, permissionKey, projectId, actorType, actorId, onBehalfOfType, onBehalfOfId, origin, redeem, requiredMode, status, satisfiedBy, approverType, approverId, expiresAt, decidedAt, settledAt and createdAt. Detail adds input, result, details and decisions[]. Counts answer `{ total, unscoped, projects: [{ projectId, slug, pending }] }`. List query supports status, projectId, permissionKey, jobId, mine, current and size; response is `{ total, current, size, hasNext, hasPrev, records }`. Seven statuses: pending, approved, rejected, expired, cancelled, executed, failed. Live payload: `{ id, type, projectId, requestId, status, at }`, type approval_request.

userStories.title: Unified inbox list
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add global and project engine inbox pages with summary rows, pagination, query-selected details and resilient refresh.

**Motivation** — Those adapters cover only the two fleet keys (`fleet.job.shell.escalate` and `fleet.budget.override`).

**Approach** — **The list API does not return fleet detail fields; details load for the open row.**
- `ApprovalRequestSummaryDto` has no `input`, `jobId` or `details`. The inbox shows each row from summary fields:
  - the key label;
  - the requester;
  - the project;
  - the countdown.
- It fetches `GET /approvals/:id` only for the row it opens.

**Project names in the global inbox.** `/approvals` resolves a row's slug from `useFleetRepos().loadProjects()` (`GET /projects`), the list the old admin inbox used. A row whose project is not in that list shows its `projectId`. A row with `projectId: null` shows `approvals.inbox.noProject`.

**Requester names.** A user requester shows the name that a lookup resolves, else their id:
- `useProjectMemberNames(slug)` on `/[project]/approvals`;
- `useAdminUsers()` on `/approvals`. It needs `user.read`, so a caller without it sees ids.

An agent requester shows its id.

**Project inbox.** `/[project]/approvals` resolves the project id from `GET /projects/:slug` (`useProjectRef(slug)`) and lists with `projectId=<id>`. `/approvals` lists everything the caller can see, with no project filter.

**Row status labels.** Rows on the All tab show their status through `approvals.inbox.status.<status>` (US-002), for all seven engine statuses. The fleet `fleet.approvals.status` keys are not reused.

**`ApprovalRequestInbox` props.** `base: { kind: 'all' } | { kind: 'project'; slug: string; projectId: string }`. The project page renders it once `useProjectRef` has the id.

**Composable imports.** Components import the new composables explicitly from `~/composables/...`, so the spec harness doubles them through module aliases (`tests/helpers/mount-sfc.ts` has a closed auto-import list).

**Live updates and polling.**
- The project inbox, the job page, the budget banner and the badge (on a project page) reload on the project stream's `approval_request` event.
- The engine publishes no event for a request without a project, so the global inbox reloads on a timer. Every list here polls through the existing visible-tab poller, as the old inbox and badge did.

Create components/approvals/ApprovalRequestInbox.vue, pages/approvals.vue and pages/[project]/approvals.vue using the US-001 client. Pending sends status=pending,size=100 and sorts soonest expiry first; All sends size=20, omits status and supports current-page navigation. Each row displays the translated/fallback permission key, requester, project and countdown. Opening fetches detail and updates ?id while preserving unrelated query entries; support entry via ?id. Provide the open-detail rendering location for US-003's panel wiring, not an old fleet panel. Use useVisiblePolling, useApprovalCountdown and a 300 ms createDebouncer for project live reloads. A 403 list shows approvals.inbox.forbidden. An initial other error toasts extractApiError and shows approvals.inbox.loadFailed; a later error preserves rows and shows approvals.inbox.stale. Detail error toasts extractApiError, closes the row and clears id. Project resolution error toasts extractApiError and never lists approvals. Cosmetic lookup errors fall back to ids. Add approvals.inbox in both locales: title, tabs, row labels, seven status labels, pager, noProject, forbidden, loadFailed, stale and empty. Mount real pages with $api doubles for endpoint/query seams; register real approvals children via mountSfc components.

**Scope** — In: new pages/list, lookup fallbacks, selection/query, polling/live and list failures. Out: real decision panel/submission (US-003), fleet panels/outcomes (US-004), badge/nav (US-006), redirect/deletion of old pages (US-010). The old inbox's keyboard shortcuts (j/k, Enter, A/D, Esc), a key filter, agent names and names beyond useAdminUsers' first page are not carried over.

**Interface** — `ApprovalRequestInbox` receives `base: { kind: 'all' } | { kind: 'project'; slug: string; projectId: string }`; use `buildRequestQuery`, `sortPendingRequests`, `requestKeyLabel`, `useApprovalInbox`, `useProjectRef` and `ProjectEventHandlers.onApprovalRequest` from US-001.

Creates `components/approvals/ApprovalRequestPanel.vue`: the frozen input, the decisions, Approve, Reject with a comment, and Cancel, each per `viewerActions`.

`ApprovalRequestInbox.vue` (created by US-002) is changed here to render the panel for the open row, and to run decide and cancel with their failure handling.

Show frozen input as indented JSON text through interpolation and decision deciderId/decision/comment as text. Generic keys post approve/reject with optional trimmed nonblank comment; reject with blank comment omits it. Both actions use buildCommentSchema(t), and overlong input posts nothing. userStories.title: Fleet panels and settled outcomes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add engine-specific bash and budget decision panels and settled delivery/requeue outcomes.

**Motivation** — Those adapters cover only the two fleet keys (`fleet.job.shell.escalate` and `fleet.budget.override`).

**Approach** — **Engine decision bodies for the fleet keys.** Bodies follow each command's `parseDecision` (`apps/api/src/fleet/approvals/commands/`):

| Choice | Body |
|:--|:--|
| bash Allow | `{ decision: 'approve', params: { choice: 'allow' } }` |
| bash Allow for this job | `{ decision: 'approve', params: { choice: 'allow_for_job' } }` |
| bash Deny | `{ decision: 'reject', params: { choice: 'deny' } }` |
| budget Raise | `{ decision: 'approve', params: { amountUsd: <number>, requeueJobIds: [<ids>] } }` (`requeueJobIds` always sent, `[]` when none is ticked) |
| budget Keep paused | `{ decision: 'reject' }` |
| any other key | `{ decision: 'approve' \| 'reject' }` |

Every body may carry a trimmed, non-blank `comment` of at most `MAX_REQUEST_COMMENT = 2000` characters, the engine DTO's limit.

Every panel validates its comment with the zod schema `buildCommentSchema(t)` from `lib/approval-requests.ts`, as `web.md` asks for schema-backed forms. The budget panel validates with `buildBudgetRaiseSchema(t, spentUsd)` from `lib/approval-request-fleet.ts`: the amount through `raiseAmountError`, the comment through the same 2000-character rule.

**Fleet payloads parse with the existing pure helpers.** Validation is not duplicated:
- a bash request's `input.payload` goes through `bashPayload({ type: 'nax_bash_escalate', payload })`;
- a budget request's `input` goes through `budgetPayload({ type: 'budget_override_required', payload: input })`.
- The bash delivery state goes through `deliveryView({ type: 'nax_bash_escalate', resolvedBy: details.resolvedBy, outcome: details.outcome })`.
- These helpers stay in `lib/fleet-approvals.ts` after US-010.

Creates `lib/approval-request-fleet.ts`, `components/approvals/ApprovalRequestBashPanel.vue`, `components/approvals/ApprovalRequestBudgetPanel.vue` and `components/approvals/ApprovalRequestOutcome.vue`.

`ApprovalRequestPanel.vue` (created by US-003) is changed here to pick the bash or budget panel with `requestPanelKind`, and to show the outcome of a settled request.

Specialized pending controls still follow viewerActions and busy state; generic keys keep US-003 behavior. Bash renders its command and available safe payload fields as text, uses bashChoices so malformed/truncated asks are deny-only, displays countdown and links to details.jobId only when project slug is known. Budget shows frozen scope through scopeText with raw scopeId, window, spend and amount; defaults every requeue candidate selected, supports unchecking and shows truncation. Raise must exceed frozen spentUsd; Keep paused needs no raise amount but still validates comment. Adapt delivery through deliveryView and requeue errors through requeueFailure. Render settled outcomes without mutation controls. Add approvals.fleet labels for panels, truncated candidates, delivery and requeue results in both locales. Tests mount the real ApprovalRequestPanel with actual specialized children through components and assert exact engine post bodies.

**Scope** — In: fleet engine parsing/body/schema helpers, specialized panel selection, bash/budget forms and outcomes. Out: generic submission orchestration (US-003), job/banner cutover (US-007), removing old panels/helpers (US-010). Budget scope names, settled-bash delivery refetching and the raised resumedAmountUsd line are deferred.

**Interface** — `requestPanelKind`, `bashAskOf`, `budgetAskOf`, `requeueCandidatesOf`, `bashRequestBody`, `budgetRaiseBody`, `budgetKeepBody`, `buildBudgetRaiseSchema`, `requestDelivery`, `requestRequeueResults`. Bash details: `{ kind: 'bash', jobId, resolvedBy, outcome }`; bash frozen input: `{ jobId, leaseEpoch, naxAskId, payload }`. Budget details: `{ kind: 'budget', policyId, resolvedBy, outcome, requeueCandidates?: [{ jobId, projectId, feature, queuedAt }], requeueCandidatesTruncated? }`; candidates exist only while pending. Budget input: `{ policyId, scopeType, scopeId, windowKind, windowStart, spentUsd, amountUsd, requestedAt }`. Budget outcome: resumedAmountUsd and `requeueResults: [{ jobId, ok, error? }]`; only the requeue results are displayed.

userStories.title: Engine approval toasts and home needs-you card
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Source approval toasts/browser notices from the engine and link home approval rows into unified inboxes.

**Motivation** — An agent write that a policy holds for a human (any of the 126 gated routes) shows up in no web inbox.

**Approach** — **The badge counts what the list lists.** `GET /approvals/counts` counts visible pending requests, the caller's own included, so the badge can count an own request the caller cannot decide. That is accepted: the badge, the Pending tab and the home card agree on one number (7a's rule).

**Key labels.** `requestKeyLabel(t, te, key)` answers `approvals.keys.<key with '.' replaced by '_'>` when that i18n key exists, else the raw key. Only the two fleet keys get labels in this feature.

Creates `composables/useApprovalRequestNotifications.ts`, which replaces what `useApprovalNotifications` does, over `GET /approvals?status=pending`.

`HomeNeedsYou` links rows to the engine inbox and labels rows with no fleet type by key.

userStories.title: Global approval policy page and shared policy UI
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Build reusable policy administration components and the global approval policy page.

**Motivation** — The redesign doc (§6 "P3 pages") asks for three pages.

**Approach** — **Policy pages share one dialog, one list and one composable.** All three are parameterised by `PolicyBase = { kind: 'global' } | { kind: 'project'; slug: string }`, so US-009 adds only a page.
- `useApprovalPolicies(base).list()` reads every page with `size: '100'` until `hasNext` is false, so `overrideCount` counts every policy.
- The dialog creates subjects of kind `all`, `type` and `role`. The `role` kind is offered only when the caller can read roles: `role.read` on the global page (`GET /roles`), project `member.read` on the project page (`GET /projects/:slug/roles`). Creating a `principal` subject is out of scope; existing ones still list.
- The dialog's mode options are `modeOptions(patternFloor(pattern, keys))`. A pattern that covers no approvable key (`patternFloor` answers `null`) shows `approvals.policies.validation.pattern`, and Save stays disabled.
- Editing changes only:
  - `mode`;
  - `timeoutSec` (a blank timeout sends `null`);
  - `onTimeout`;
  - `approverMustHoldAction`;
  - `requireDistinctApprover`.

  The pattern and the subject are part of the policy's selector, and `PATCH` does not accept them.

The API's policy validation (`apps/api/src/approvals/approval-policy.validation.ts`):
- `timeoutSec` must be an integer from 60 to 2592000;
- `onTimeout: 'approve'` needs floor `none`;
- the mode may not sit below the strictest floor of the keys the pattern covers. A `prefix.*` pattern covers the keys under `prefix.`, and a pattern that covers none is refused.

Create lib/approval-policies.ts, composables/useApprovalPolicies.ts, components/approvals/ApprovalPolicyDialog.vue, ApprovalPolicyList.vue, ApprovableKeysTable.vue and pages/admin/approval-policies.vue. The shared components/composable must already support project endpoint/role selection for US-009. Global reads/writes require approval.policy.manage; absent permission renders approvals.policies.forbidden and requests nothing. Keys table shows key, scope, risk, floor, default and overrideCount over every policy page. Use exact/prefix.* matching, rank none<self<agent<human, strictest matching floor and schema-backed forms; API validation remains authoritative.

Create subjects all/type/role, offering role only with the appropriate read permission and successful useRoles/useProjectRoles loading. A failed role load simply removes that kind. Existing principal-subject policies remain displayable/editable/deletable, but no principal-create UI. Blank create timeout is omitted; blank edit timeout sends null. Patch only the five listed mutable fields, not requiredApprovals even though the API DTO accepts it, and never pattern/subject. Delete requires confirmation. Refusals 400/403/409 toast extractApiError and preserve the open dialog and input. Load 403 shows approvals.policies.forbidden. Add approvals.policies in both locales, including page, keys table, list, dialog, subject, validation and forbidden messages. Tests use real page/dialog/list with $api doubles to verify global calls and exact bodies, plus pure matching/schema cases and pagination.

**Scope** — In: all shared global/project policy machinery, global page/CRUD and owning locale/tests. Out: project page/inherited-page integration (US-009), navigation links (US-006), API changes, principal subject creation, role subject when role reading fails.

**Interface** — `PolicyBase = { kind: 'global' } | { kind: 'project'; slug: string }`; `patternFloor`, `modeOptions`, `overrideCount`, `buildPolicySchema`; `useApprovalPolicies`; `ApprovalPolicyDialog`, `ApprovalPolicyList`, `ApprovableKeysTable`. Global routes: GET/POST `/approval-policies`, PATCH/DELETE `/approval-policies/:id`, GET `/approval-policies/keys` answering `{ keys }`. Project equivalents: GET/POST `/projects/:slug/approval-policies`, PATCH/DELETE `/projects/:slug/approval-policies/:id`, GET `/projects/:slug/approval-policies/keys`. Policy fields: id, selector, projectId, permissionPattern, principalType, roleId, principalId, mode, timeoutSec, onTimeout, requiredApprovals, approverMustHoldAction, requireDistinctApprover, updatedByType, updatedById, createdAt, updatedAt. `ApprovableKeyDto`: `key`, `scope`, `risk`, `floor`, `default`. Modes rank `none < self < agent < human`. The default example create body is exactly `{ permissionPattern: 'label.create', appliesTo: { kind: 'type', principalType: 'AGENT' }, mode: 'human', onTimeout: 'reject' }`; untouched optional controls must not add unexpected default fields.
